edges.description: Corticospinal tract degeneration disinhibits spinal stretch reflexes, producing progressive limb spasticity.
Bilateral corticospinal tract degeneration produces progressive lower-limb spasticity and pyramidal paraparesis.
Lower-extremity pyramidal spasticity produces a characteristic stiff, spastic gait.
Loss of descending corticospinal inhibition causes generalized hyperreflexia.
Pyramidal corticospinal tract dysfunction releases the extensor plantar response (Babinski sign).
Cervical corticospinal tract disinhibition releases the upper-limb finger flexor reflex (Hoffmann sign).
Loss of upper motor neuron drive produces pyramidal weakness in voluntary muscle movement.
Corticobulbar tract degeneration produces spastic dysarthria and progressive loss of motor speech production.
Corticobulbar upper motor neuron dysfunction impairs voluntary and pharyngeal swallowing control.
Lower-limb spasticity and pyramidal motor dysfunction impair balance and gait.
Corticobulbar and fronto-pontocerebellar disconnection produces emotional lability (pseudobulbar affect).
Loss of supraspinal corticospinal modulation of sacral micturition centers causes bladder instability and urinary urgency.
intermediate_mechanisms: Supraspinal disinhibition of sacral micturition reflex pathways

edges.description: Cerebellar and cerebro-cerebellar network dysfunction exacerbates gait and balance impairment in PLS.
Cerebellar cortical and dentate nuclear atrophy impairs limb dexterity and motor coordination.
Cerebellar pathology compounds bulbar motor speech impairment.
Cerebello-frontal disconnection contributes to emotional lability and pseudobulbar affect.
